edges.description: Loss of functional K85 protein or failure of K85-K35 heterodimeric filament assembly directly disrupts keratin intermediate filament bundling in differentiating hair follicle cortical and cuticle cells.
Loss of functional KRT85 intermediate filaments in nail-forming epithelium directly impairs hard keratinization in the nail matrix.
Defective K85-K35 keratin filament assembly in early differentiating hair cortical cells impairs hair formation and causes congenital hypotrichosis.
Disruption of K85-K35 intermediate filament bundling prevents normal cortical filament organization and results in structurally abnormal, fragile hair shafts.
Severe disruption of KRT85 function in the hair matrix and cuticle leads to failure of hair shaft production and complete alopecia.
Defective keratinization in nail matrix keratinocytes directly produces dystrophic, brittle, and malformed nail plates.

nodes.description: Structural abnormalities and brittleness of the hair shaft reflecting disrupted K85-K35 keratin intermediate filament organization within the early differentiating hair cortex and cuticle.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal recessive transmission of a rare KRT74 variant causes hair and nail ectodermal dysplasia: allelism with dominant woolly hair/hypotrichosis.
evidence.snippet: Pure hair and nail ectodermal dysplasia (PHNED) comprises a heterogeneous group of rare heritable disorders characterized by brittle hair, hypotrichosis, onychodystrophy and micronychia. Autosomal recessive (AR) PHNED has previously been associated with mutations in either KRT85 or HOXC13 on chromosome 12p11.1-q14.3.

nodes.description: Congenital or progressive complete loss of scalp and body hair. Complete alopecia has been reported with severe KRT85 mutations, including the homozygous R78H missense mutation in the head domain.

evidence.reference_title: De novo filament formation by human hair keratins K85 and K35 follows a filament development pattern distinct from cytokeratin filament networks.
evidence.snippet: The former mutation results in more severe phenotypes (complete alopecia and severe nail dystrophy) than the latter mutation

nodes.description: Within the hair matrix, cuticle, and early differentiating hair cortex, K85-K35 heterodimers normally form short intermediate filaments that bundle into proto-macrofibrils. Disruption of KRT85 prevents normal cortical and cuticle keratin filament bundling, resulting in structurally fragile hair shafts, sparse hair (hypotrichosis), or complete failure of hair shaft production (alopecia).

nodes.description: KRT85 encodes keratin 85 (formerly KRTHB5), a type II hard keratin that obligately heterodimerizes with type I hair keratins (particularly KRT35) to form short intermediate filaments that laterally associate into bundles. Transcription of KRT85 and KRT35 is directly activated upstream by HOXC13 (mutated in ECTD9). Biallelic pathogenic variants in KRT85 either abolish K85-K35 filament assembly into cytoplasmic aggregates (such as the tail-domain delCT frameshift) or alter conserved head-domain residues required for higher-order filament organization (such as R78H), compromising hard keratin intermediate filament integrity across both hair follicle and nail matrix epithelia.
